title: Rook and the Wobbly Bridge
markdown:
Whoooo could have guessed that a little goblin named Rook might be so fond of a tiny kitten? Rook lived in the Hollowpeak Hills. The moonbeams made silver threads in the trees. The air smelled like damp earth and sleepy wildflowers. His kitten, oh, his kitten was named Fluffernutter. Fluffernutter had fur as white and soft as a brand-new snowdrift. His paws tiptoed as if walking on the quietest whisper.

Now, Rook loved Fluffernutter more than sparkly pebbles he found by the creek. He loved him more than the crunchiest roots dug from the ground. He loved him as much as the tallest trees love the biggest moonbeams. One evening, the moon climbed high. It painted the world in soft, hazy light. "Come, Fluffernutter," Rook whispered. His voice was as soft and gentle as a moth's wing brushing a petal. "We shall explore the little silver forest just past Whisperwind Creek."

Rook’s heart, though, fluttered a little. This was nervousness, Rook thought. You see, there was a tiny bridge over Whisperwind Creek. It was made of twisty, shimmering silver vines that twinkled like a necklace of stars. Some older goblins, with their gruff voices and wide shoulders, muttered that it was a bit wobbly. They said it swayed too much when the wind played its games. But Rook knew, deep in his goblin heart, a place as true as the north star, that it was perfectly safe. He wanted to prove it, especially to his dear Fluffernutter, who sometimes looked a little hesitant at new things.

As they padded along the mossy path, the trees whispered secrets to each other. Their leaves rustled like pages in an old book. The stars twinkled above, like spilled sugar across a dark velvet cloth. Soon, they heard the gentle gurgle of Whisperwind Creek. It sounded like a happy sigh. And there it was, the little silver bridge, glistening under the moon. Its vines caught the light and sent little sparkles dancing in the air. It looked quite beautiful.

Then, a soft puff of wind, no bigger than a sigh from a sleeping badger, blew past them. It tickled Rook’s ears and made the leaves on the trees dance. The bridge swayed, just a whisper, a tiny ripple. Rook’s breath hitched, just a little, a tiny gasp. This was doubt, Rook realised. He felt a small, insistent paw patting his ankle, and then another. It was Fluffernutter, looking up at him with his big, curious, emerald-green eyes.

Rook fumbled for his map. It was a very old map, a smudged map. It had helpful drawings that were not so helpful now. He saw a squiggly line for the creek, and then... a drawing of a mountain lantern. A mountain lantern? What good was a mountain lantern when you were standing by a little silver bridge? His own confidence flickered like a candle in a sudden breeze, threatening to go out. He felt a wave of worry.

Patience now. All will be revealed in time. The trees remember this story well. Rook suddenly thought of Barnaby Buttercrust. Barnaby was the kindest goblin baker in all the Hollowpeak Hills. Barnaby was round like a perfectly risen bun, with flour always dusted on his nose. His smile could melt a grumpy glacier. Barnaby always said, with a twinkle in his eye, "A little courage, Rook, is like a warm loaf on a chilly morning. It fills you up and makes everything feel better. And it helps you share your warmth with others."

Taking a deep breath, Rook gently scooped Fluffernutter into his arms. He tucked the soft kitten close to his chest. Fluffernutter’s fur felt like holding a moonbeam. "It's alright, little one," he murmured. His voice was steady now, like a flowing stream. "We'll just try one step. Just one brave little step." He placed one small, earth-brown, booted foot onto the silver vines of the bridge. The silver vines felt cool and slightly rough beneath his boot. The wood creaked with a low groan. The scent of damp moss rose around him. But the bridge held him firm. Fluffernutter, nestled in his arms, began to purr. A rumbling, happy sound that vibrated through Rook's chest. This was reassurance, Rook thought.

One step. Then another. The bridge swayed again, but this time it felt like a friendly little dance, a gentle sway under the watchful moon. Rook’s worries melted away like frost in the morning sun. They reached the other side, and the forest floor felt solid and welcoming beneath their feet. The trees themselves seemed to rustle with approval, their leaves whispering a song of encouragement.

Rook looked down at Fluffernutter, who was now batting playfully at a dangling moonbeam. His tail twitched with delight. Rook smiled a wide, goblin smile. It showed all his little, slightly crooked teeth. The bridge was safe, just as he thought. Sometimes, Rook realised, what seems a little wobbly is only so because we haven't tried it with a brave heart and a purring friend by our side. The world felt a little bit bigger and a lot more wonderful. This was discovery, Rook felt.

And so, Rook and Fluffernutter continued their moonlit stroll. Their steps were light and sure, no longer hesitant. The path home felt welcoming, and the idea of warm beds and sweet dreams of moonlit adventures was a delightful prospect. Thus, it is known among the forest folk that courage, like a perfectly baked bun, can lead to the most comforting and happy of journeys.
characters: Rook the young goblin, a kitten
